**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**

**New York City, NY --- November 8th, 2026** --- The nation's top environmental watchdog, Green Transit Alliance (GTA) keeps track of public transit emissions using the GTA Value Index (GTA VI). Each year, the three agencies with the highest GTA VI's are given 'Green Awards' according to agency size: small, medium, and large. However, this year, GTA also decided to sling a bit of mud at the nation's lowest performers by offering 'Brown Awards" for high emissions. Let's dive into the data and see where the water is  crystal clear and also where it gets murky.

## Data Acquisition and Preparation

```{r}
#| output: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

#Task 1a: Data Acquisition - State Electricity Profiles
# ***Instructor's code*** #
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)

get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
    library(tidyverse)
    library(stringr)
    library(httr2)
    library(rvest)
    library(fs)
  
    state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
    
    dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
    file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
    
    fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
    
    if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
        BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
        RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
          req_url_path("electricity", 
                       "state", 
                       state_formatted) |>
          req_headers(
            `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>   
          req_retry(
                max_tries = 4, 
          ) |>
          req_perform(file_name)
    
        resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
    }
    
    TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
        html_element("table") |> 
        html_table() |>
        mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
    
    if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
        TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
    }
    
    CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |> 
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
        pull(Rank)
    
    RATE <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        as.numeric()
    
    GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
               primary_source        = PRIMARY,
               electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
               # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
               generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
               state                 = state, 
               abbreviation          = abbr
    )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()

# ***My code*** #
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)

#Format columns and apply gt styles
EIA_SEP_REPORT |> 
  mutate(
    State = paste0(state, ", (", abbreviation, ")")
  ) |> 
  select(
    `CO2 Emitted Per MWh of Electricity Produced (lbs)` = CO2_MWh,
    `Primary Source of Electricity Generation` = primary_source,
    `Average Retail Price (per MWh)` = electricity_price_MWh,
    `Total Generation Capacity (MWh)` = generation_MWh,
    State
  ) |> 
  # Turn it into a gt table object
  gt() |> 
  # Format the price column as currency ($XX.XX)
  fmt_currency(
    columns = `Average Retail Price (per MWh)`,
    decimals = 2
  ) |> 
  # Add commas per 1,000 increment for the total capacity
  fmt_integer(
    columns = `Total Generation Capacity (MWh)`,
    use_seps = TRUE
  )


```

```{r}
#Task 1b: Data Acquisition - NTD Energy Usage
# ***Instructor's code*** #
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()


```

```{r}
#Task 1c: Data Acquisition - Transit Service Provided
# ***Instructor's code*** #
load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```

## Exploratory Data Analysis 
```{r}
#| message: false

#Task 3a: Initial Analysis of SEP Data
#Question 1
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Filter out the top 5 most expensive states
top_5_expensive <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> 
  slice_max(electricity_price_MWh, n = 5)

# 2. Build the bar chart
ggplot(top_5_expensive, aes(x = electricity_price_MWh, y = reorder(state, electricity_price_MWh))) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkgreen") +
  # Add labels to the ends of the bars formatted as currency
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::dollar(electricity_price_MWh)), 
            hjust = -0.1, fontface = "bold") +
  # Expand the x-axis limits slightly to ensure labels don't get cut off
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar_format(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 5 States with the Most Expensive Electricity Prices",
    x = "Average Retail Price (per MWh)",
    y = "State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11)
  )
```
Here, we can clearly see Hawaii tops the chart by far as the most expensive place to charge your phone.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

# 1. Filter top 5 states and calculate row-wide color hex codes
top_5_dirty <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> 
  slice_max(CO2_MWh, n = 5) |> 
  mutate(
    State = paste0(state, ", (", abbreviation, ")"),
    row_color = scales::col_numeric(palette = c("#F5F5DC", "#8B4513"), domain = NULL)(CO2_MWh)
  ) |> 
  select(
    `CO2 Emitted Per MWh of Electricity Produced (lbs)` = CO2_MWh,
    `Primary Source of Electricity Generation` = primary_source,
    `Average Retail Price (per MWh)` = electricity_price_MWh,
    `Total Generation Capacity (MWh)` = generation_MWh,
    State,
    row_color
  )

# 2. Build table structure and apply text/number formatting
dirty_table <- top_5_dirty |> 
  select(-row_color) |> 
  gt() |> 
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Top 5 States with the Dirtiest Electricity Mixes**"), # Bold Title
    subtitle = md("*Ranked by highest pounds of CO2 emitted per Megawatthour (MWh)*") # Italic Subtitle
  ) |> 
  fmt_currency(columns = `Average Retail Price (per MWh)`, decimals = 2) |> 
  fmt_integer(columns = c(`Total Generation Capacity (MWh)`, `CO2 Emitted Per MWh of Electricity Produced (lbs)`), use_seps = TRUE) |> 
  
  # 3. Style Header Block (Grey background and bold labels)
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "#EFEFEF"), # Clean light grey background
      cell_text(weight = "bold")    # Bold lettering
    ),
    locations = list(
      cells_column_labels(columns = everything()), # Bold all column labels
      cells_title(groups = "title")                # Apply to title block
    )
  )

# 4. Apply the synchronized brown colors to each body row
for(i in 1:nrow(top_5_dirty)) {
  dirty_table <- dirty_table |> 
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = top_5_dirty$row_color[i], alpha = 0.5),
      locations = cells_body(rows = i)
    )
}

# Display the styled table
dirty_table
```

Surprisingly, Hawaii strikes again! It would seem that high prices aren't always a sign of luxury or quality.

On average, **`r round(us_weighted_co2, 1)`** pounds of CO2 are emitted per MWh of electricity produced in the US. Multiply that by the total number of MWh produced annually and you can start to see why climate scientists have been sounding the alarm for decades. Yikes!

```{r}
#Task 3b: Explore NTD Energy Data
#Question 1
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

# 1. Identify fuel gallon columns, calculate row-wide totals, and find top 5 agencies
top_5_fuel_agencies <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  # Compute total physical gallons per row across all fuel columns containing "Gallons"
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    row_total_gallons = sum(c_across(contains("Gallons")), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  # Group strictly by agency name to combine modes (e.g., combining their Motorbus & Vanpool)
  group_by(`Agency Name`) |>
  summarize(
    `Diesel (Gallons)`           = sum(`Gallons of Diesel Fuel`, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Gasoline (Gallons)`         = sum(`Gallons of Gasoline`, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Compressed Nat. Gas (CNG)`  = sum(`Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Total Gallons (All Fuel)`   = sum(row_total_gallons, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  # Isolate the top 5 highest consumers
  slice_max(`Total Gallons (All Fuel)`, n = 5) |>
  # Assign blue gradient row-by-row based on fuel intensity
  mutate(
    row_color = scales::col_numeric(palette = "Blues", domain = NULL)(`Total Gallons (All Fuel)`)
  )

# 2. Render the formatted gt table
fuel_table <- top_5_fuel_agencies |>
  select(-row_color) |> # Drop helper column from visual layout
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Top 5 Transit Agencies by Total Fuel Consumption**"),
    subtitle = md("*Consumption breakdown for gallons of liquid fuel and natural gas*")
  ) |>
  # Add comma formatting for all numeric columns
  fmt_integer(
    columns = where(is.numeric),
    use_seps = TRUE
  ) |>
  # Style header block: Bold labels with light grey background
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "#EFEFEF"),
      cell_text(weight = "bold")
    ),
    locations = list(
      cells_column_labels(columns = everything()),
      cells_title(groups = "title")
    )
  )

# 3. Apply uniform row-wide colors with light opacity for readability
for(i in 1:nrow(top_5_fuel_agencies)) {
  fuel_table <- fuel_table |>
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = top_5_fuel_agencies$row_color[i], alpha = 0.5),
      locations = cells_body(rows = i)
    )
}

# Display the final table
fuel_table
```
Nothing too unusual here. Dense population centers tend to have complex transit systems that are more robustly used, so these numbers seem pretty reasonable.

## Data Analysis
**Calculate Total Emissions**
```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

#Task 5: Calculate Emissions
#MASTER_TABLE set up
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Prepare NTD_SERVICE anchor data (Agency + Mode Pair + State)
service_anchor <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  select(NTD_ID, AGENCY, state, mode) |>
  distinct()

# 2. Prepare NTD_ENERGY data, fix the ID type mismatch, and DROP the duplicate agency column
energy_clean <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  rename(NTD_ID = `NTD ID`, mode = Mode) |>
  # Convert ID from double to character to match NTD_SERVICE string type
  mutate(NTD_ID = as.character(NTD_ID)) |> 
  # FIX: Drop the extra Agency Name column so it doesn't conflict during the join
  select(-`Agency Name`)

# 3. Prepare EIA_SEP_REPORT data 
eia_clean <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  select(
    state_abb = abbreviation, 
    `EIA CO2 Emitted (lbs/MWh)` = CO2_MWh
  )

# 4. Execute the multi-stage Master Table join pipeline
MASTER_TABLE <- service_anchor |>
  # Step A: Connect fuel metrics using the paired matching keys
  left_join(energy_clean, by = c("NTD_ID", "mode")) |>
  
  # Step B: Connect EIA CO2 emissions by matching the transit state to EIA state
  left_join(eia_clean, by = c("state" = "state_abb")) |>
  
  # Step C: Refine layout structure
  select(
    `Agency Name` = AGENCY,
    Mode = mode,
    `State Location` = state,
    everything()
  ) |>
  # Keep only pairs that have valid recording inputs
  filter(!is.na(`Agency Name`))

#Add total emissions
library(tidyverse)

# Helper function to safely fetch a column by string pattern without crashing if missing
get_fuel_val <- function(df, pattern) {
  cols <- df |> select(matches(pattern))
  if (ncol(cols) > 0) rowSums(cols, na.rm = TRUE) else 0
}

# Execute master table emissions calculations using pattern matching
MASTER_TABLE_WITH_EMISSIONS <- MASTER_TABLE |>
  # 1. First replace all NA values globally across numeric fields with 0
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace_na(.x, 0))) |>
  
  # 2. Add total emissions using safe pattern searches
  mutate(
    `Total CO2 Emissions (lbs)` = 
      (get_fuel_val(pick(everything()), "Diesel") * 22.45) + 
      (get_fuel_val(pick(everything()), "Gasoline") * 18.73) + 
      (get_fuel_val(pick(everything()), "Petroleum|LPG") * 12.68) + 
      (get_fuel_val(pick(everything()), "Liquefied Natural Gas|LNG") * 10.15) + 
      (get_fuel_val(pick(everything()), "Compressed|CNG") * 0.12) + 
      (get_fuel_val(pick(everything()), "Kilowatt|Electricity|kWh") * (`EIA CO2 Emitted (lbs/MWh)` / 1000))
  )

```
**Relate Total Emissions and Passenger Service**
```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

#Task 6: Normalize Emissions to Transit Usage
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Prepare NTD_SERVICE anchor data and align the mode codes to full text names
service_anchor <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID = as.numeric(NTD_ID),
    # FIX: Recode mode here too so it matches NTD_ENERGY perfectly!
    mode = recode_values(mode, 
                         "HR" ~ "Heavy Rail", 
                         "LR" ~ "Light Rail",
                         "CR" ~ "Commuter Rail",
                         "MG" ~ "Monorail / Automated Guideway",
                         "SR" ~ "Streetcar Rail",
                         "IP" ~ "Inclined Plane",
                         "CC" ~ "Cable Car",
                         "MB" ~ "Motorbus",
                         "CB" ~ "Commuter Bus",
                         "RB" ~ "Bus Rapid Transit",
                         "TB" ~ "Trolleybus",
                         "FB" ~ "Ferryboat",
                         "TR" ~ "Aerial Tramway",
                         "DR" ~ "Demand Response",
                         "DT" ~ "Demand Response Taxi",
                         "JT" ~ "Jitney",
                         "VP" ~ "Vanpool",
                         "PB" ~ "Publico",
                         "OR" ~ "Other Rail",
                         default = "Unknown"
    )
  ) |>
  select(NTD_ID, AGENCY, state, mode) |>
  distinct()

# 2. Prepare NTD_ENERGY data
energy_clean <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  rename(NTD_ID = `NTD ID`, mode = Mode) |>
  mutate(NTD_ID = as.numeric(NTD_ID)) |> 
  select(-`Agency Name`)

# 3. Prepare EIA_SEP_REPORT data 
eia_clean <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
  select(
    state_abb = abbreviation, 
    `EIA CO2 Emitted (lbs/MWh)` = CO2_MWh
  )

# 4. Re-join the Master Table with synchronized keys
MASTER_TABLE <- service_anchor |>
  left_join(energy_clean, by = c("NTD_ID", "mode")) |>
  left_join(eia_clean, by = c("state" = "state_abb")) |>
  select(
    `Agency Name` = AGENCY,
    Mode = mode,
    `State Location` = state,
    everything()
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(`Agency Name`))

# 5. Clean up NAs globally across the matched numeric fields
MASTER_TABLE_WITH_EMISSIONS <- MASTER_TABLE |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~replace_na(.x, 0)))

# Helper column index finder for safety
safe_col <- function(df, pattern) {
  col_idx <- grep(pattern, colnames(df), ignore.case = TRUE)
  if (length(col_idx) > 0) {
    if (length(col_idx) > 1) rowSums(df[, col_idx], na.rm = TRUE) else df[[col_idx]]
  } else {
    rep(0, nrow(df))
  }
}

# 6. Re-calculate row-wide total emissions
MASTER_TABLE_WITH_EMISSIONS$`Total CO2 Emissions (lbs)` <- 
  (safe_col(MASTER_TABLE_WITH_EMISSIONS, "Diesel") * 22.45) + 
  (safe_col(MASTER_TABLE_WITH_EMISSIONS, "Gasoline") * 18.73) + 
  (safe_col(MASTER_TABLE_WITH_EMISSIONS, "Petroleum|LPG") * 12.68) + 
  (safe_col(MASTER_TABLE_WITH_EMISSIONS, "Liquefied Natural Gas|LNG") * 10.15) + 
  (safe_col(MASTER_TABLE_WITH_EMISSIONS, "Compressed|CNG") * 0.12) + 
  (safe_col(MASTER_TABLE_WITH_EMISSIONS, "Kilowatt|Electricity|kWh") * 
     (MASTER_TABLE_WITH_EMISSIONS$`EIA CO2 Emitted (lbs/MWh)` / 1000))
################
library(gt)

# 1. Aggregate emissions by Agency and capture State Location
agency_efficiency <- MASTER_TABLE_WITH_EMISSIONS |>
  group_by(`Agency Name`) |>
  summarize(
    State = first(`State Location`),
    Total_Emissions_lbs = sum(`Total CO2 Emissions (lbs)`, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  # 2. Join with transit metrics from NTD_SERVICE
  inner_join(
    NTD_SERVICE |>
      group_by(AGENCY) |>
      summarize(
        Total_UPT = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
        Total_Passenger_Miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ),
    by = c("Agency Name" = "AGENCY")
  ) |>
  # Filter out non-operational entries and ensure emissions are tracked
  filter(Total_UPT > 1000 & Total_Passenger_Miles > 1000 & Total_Emissions_lbs > 0) |>
  
  # 3. Compute efficiency metrics and apply size brackets
  mutate(
    Emissions_Per_UPT  = Total_Emissions_lbs / Total_UPT,
    Emissions_Per_Mile = Total_Emissions_lbs / Total_Passenger_Miles,
    
    Agency_Size = case_when(
      Total_UPT < 1e6                     ~ "Small (< 1M annual trips)",
      Total_UPT >= 1e6 & Total_UPT < 10e6 ~ "Medium (1M - 10M annual trips)",
      Total_UPT >= 10e6                   ~ "Large (> 10M annual trips)"
    )
  )

# 4. Isolate the most efficient winner per category tier
efficiency_awards <- agency_efficiency |>
  group_by(Agency_Size) |>
  slice_min(Emissions_Per_UPT, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(
    `Agency Size` = Agency_Size,
    `Agency Name`,
    State,
    `Total Annual Trips (UPT)` = Total_UPT,
    `Lbs CO2 Per Trip` = Emissions_Per_UPT,
    `Lbs CO2 Per Passenger Mile` = Emissions_Per_Mile
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(`Total Annual Trips (UPT)`))

# 5. Render the final styled award table
efficiency_awards |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Transit Efficiency Awards by Agency Size**"),
    subtitle = md("*Most efficient networks based on lowest CO2 emissions per Unlinked Passenger Trip (UPT)*")
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = list(
      cell_fill(color = "#EFEFEF"),
      cell_text(weight = "bold")
    ),
    locations = list(
      cells_column_labels(columns = everything()),
      cells_title(groups = "title")
    )
  ) |>
  fmt_integer(columns = `Total Annual Trips (UPT)`, use_seps = TRUE) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(`Lbs CO2 Per Trip`, `Lbs CO2 Per Passenger Mile`), decimals = 4)


```
**‘Greenest’ Transit Agencies**

As we can see here, California sweeps gold in all three categories! From largest to smallest by annual trips: Santa Monica, Culver City, and Redondo Beach have the greenest transit systems in the nation. Cowabunga dudes!

**'Brownest' Transit Agencies**
```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

# 1. Isolate the absolute highest efficiency winner (1 per size tier)
green_winners <- agency_efficiency |>
  group_by(Agency_Size) |>
  slice_min(Emissions_Per_UPT, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(Award_Type = "Green Award (Most Efficient)")

# 2. Isolate the single worst absolute emitter (CHANGED: 1 per size tier instead of 3)
brown_winners <- agency_efficiency |>
  group_by(Agency_Size) |>
  slice_max(Emissions_Per_UPT, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(Award_Type = "Brown Award (Highest Emissions)")

# 3. Combine the 1-vs-1 matchups
all_winners_1v1 <- bind_rows(green_winners, brown_winners) |>
  mutate(
    Graph_Label = paste0(`Agency Name`, " (", State, ")")
  )

# 4. Plot a highly legible Dot Plot with a Logarithmic Axis
ggplot(all_winners_1v1, aes(x = Emissions_Per_UPT, y = Agency_Size, color = Award_Type)) +
  # Draw a subtle background connector line between the two dots for each size group
  geom_line(aes(group = Agency_Size), color = "grey70", linewidth = 1) +
  
  # Place large, crisp comparative dots
  geom_point(size = 5, alpha = 0.9) +
  
  # Add exact numeric text labels floating right above each dot (your original code)
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.4f", Emissions_Per_UPT)), 
            vjust = -1.2, fontface = "bold", size = 3.2, show.legend = FALSE, color = "black") +
  
  # FIX / ADDED: Places the Brown Agency Name and State off to the right of the brown dots
  geom_text(data = filter(all_winners_1v1, Award_Type == "Brown Award (Highest Emissions)"),
            aes(label = Graph_Label),
            hjust = -0.1, vjust = 0.4, fontface = "italic", size = 3, color = "#8B4513", show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  # Logarithmic scale allows both huge and tiny numbers to share the same axis beautifully
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_log(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.4))) + # Expanded right margin for text padding
  
  # Map your exact custom green and brown color choices
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Green Award (Most Efficient)" = "#2E8B57", 
                                "Brown Award (Highest Emissions)" = "#8B4513")) +
  labs(
    title = "The Transit Efficiency Chasm: Green vs. Brown Winners",
    subtitle = "Comparing the 1-vs-1 extremes on a Logarithmic Scale (lbs CO2 per trip)",
    x = "Lbs CO2 Per Passenger Trip (Logarithmic)",
    y = "",
    color = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(style = "italic", size = 10),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank() # Clean up logarithmic grid clutter
  )


```
On the other end of the spectrum we have states like Alaska, Washington, and (of course) New Jersey doing everything they can to hasten humanity's demise. Like the great humanitarian Thanos once said: "Perfectly balanced, as all things should be."

## Transit Award Press Release

GTA used annual Unlinked Passenger Trips as a basis for how much CO2 agencies are emitting per trip and per passenger mile. By categorizing agencies according to ridership, GTA was able to find the three best and three worst performers in the nation. Coming in at the lowest CO2 Emissions per passenger trip and representing the medium size category is CityBus out of Culver City, CA (0.0340 lbs CO2 per passenger mile). Next, we have the large agency Big Blue Bus from Santa Monica, CA (0.053 lbs CO2 per passenger mile). To finish out the Green Awards, we have the small agency of Beach Cities Transit, out of Redondo Beach, CA (0.0618 lbs CO2 per passenger mile). Continuing our ascent through the smog, we have our third place Brown Award recipient, Washington State Ferries pumping a whopping 17.8405 lbs of CO2 into the atmosphere per passenger mile. Next highest is medium-sized Seastreak from New Jersey, leaving 43.7696 streaks of brown in the water for every passenger they carry one mile. Finally, the dirtiest dog on the block: the large and in charge Alaska Railroad Corporation with a massive ***96.7474 lbs of CO2 per passenger mile!*** For reference on just how insane that number is, the Alaska Railroad Corporation emits almost 200x more CO2 than the median large agency (0.511 lbs CO2 per passenger mile). On the other end, our winner Culver CityBus emits nearly 30x ***less*** than the median for medium-sized agencies (0.925 lbs CO2 per passenger mile)
